apps.localizedDescription:
Tethercam:

Use your iPhone as a webcam on Windows 11 or Linux, over a USB cable, at up to 4K. Free and open source.

Project page →.

Tethercam turns an iPhone into a standard Windows webcam that Teams, Zoom, OBS, Streamlabs, browsers and the Camera app can use. No account, no watermark, no overlays: plug in the cable, open the app, pick Tethercam (Windows Virtual Camera). Optionally, pair once over the cable and use it over Wi-Fi.

Status: beta. Works end to end with a real iPhone 15 Pro Max: 1080p30/60 and 4K30 through the Windows camera stack, ~100 ms glass-to-glass latency at 1080p30, hardware encode and decode. On Linux the same iPhone pairs over USB and streams 1080p60 over Wi-Fi. See MILESTONES.md for what's still open.

versions.localizedDescription: Windows: install the MSI (needs Windows 11 and the Apple Devices app). Linux: install the .deb for your Ubuntu release or the .rpm for Fedora (needs v4l2loopback; see docs/USER_GUIDE.md). iPhone: add the AltStore source https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kshitizwagle/tethercam/main/altstore/source.json, or sideload Tethercam-unsigned.ipa with Sideloadly/AltStore (signs it with your Apple ID). See README for details.

privacy.NSCameraUsageDescription: Tethercam streams your camera to your PC over the USB cable, or over Wi-Fi to PCs you paired.
privacy.NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription: With Wireless on, Tethercam lets PCs you paired over USB find your iPhone and receive its camera over Wi-Fi.
